row.notes:
### Authoring note: minimum embedded-shape contract (archived 2026-05-23)

This contract was originally stored in the (removed) `minimum_embedded_shape` column. Field-level constraints on embedded shells are now enforced by the deployer at deploy time against the canonical entity's `fields` metadata; this note is preserved as authoring intent only.

Minimum embedded-shape contract for `job_offers` — modules that embedded_master offers (`ATS-BACKGROUND-CHECKS`, `ATS-PRE-EMPLOYEE-RECORD`) need the offer-state subset:

- `id` — primary key.
- `candidate_id` — FK to `candidates`; required (offer addressee).
- `application_id` — FK to `job_applications`; required (the application this offer resolves).
- `requisition_id` — FK to `job_requisitions`; required for downstream reporting (offer-acceptance-rate by requisition).
- `state` — offer lifecycle state (`draft`, `approved`, `extended`, `accepted`, `declined`, `rescinded`); modules read this to gate their own behavior (BACKGROUND-CHECKS only runs after `extended` or `accepted`; PRE-EMPLOYEE-RECORD is only created when `state = accepted`).
- `extended_at` — required to compute time-to-accept and time-to-start metrics.

The canonical master `ATS-OFFERS` extends with compensation_components, signature_url, decline_reason, etc.

row.description: Entry-tier deployable for a basic hiring workflow: post jobs, capture applications, run interviews, and make offers. Embeds the canonical masters from the full ATS modules and inherits their lifecycle states and gated steps, which it governs under its own permission prefix. Leaves out the requisition approval chain, background-check processing, and the pre-employee record. When the full ATS modules are installed, its entities move to them without data migration.
row.catalog_tagline: Everything a small team needs to hire, in one lightweight package.
row.catalog_description: A starter bundle covering the core hiring path (postings, candidates, applications, interviews, and offers) without the breadth of the full module set. Stand up hiring quickly, then grow into the full modules as your volume increases; your data moves with you when you do.
row.specification_requirements: Hiring manager access to candidates. A `candidates` row has no relationship leading to its hiring manager, so the row-scope rule cannot admit them. As a workaround, under `access_scope: raci` the `HIRING-MANAGER` persona holds `hiring-starter:view_all_candidates`.
